Question: What is EOH?
Answer: EOH is an annual 2-day event that showcases engineering at UIUC, a tradition that has been evolving for over a century. As the largest student-run STEM fair in the country, EOH presents over 200 exhibits to approximately 35,000 visitors each year. Other key events include a Tesla Coil Concert, Build-a-Blinkie, a Keynote Speaker (past speakers include Yu Pan (YouTube, PayPal) and Todd Little (Oracle)), middle and high school design competitions, and more. Question: What are the event hours?
Answer: Exhibits are open {hours} on {dates}, unless otherwise noted due to weather. Shuttle hours are under Shuttles & parking.

Question: Where can I find help or ask questions during the event?
Answer: Visit one of our Visitor’s Booths located at the Campus Instructional Facility (CIF), in the courtyard between NCSA and Siebel Computer Science Building, outside Sidney Lu Mechanical Engineering Building, or outside the Electrical and Computer Engineering Building (ECEB).

Question: What should I do in case of severe weather?
Answer: Check the event website for updates on where exhibits will be held: https://eohillinois.org

Question: Are minors allowed to attend alone?
Answer: No. All minors must be accompanied by a parent or guardian at all times.

Question: Do you have events suitable for elementary, middle, and high schoolers?
Answer: Yes! EOH is open to everyone and we have activities suitable for all ages.

Question: Is EOH free? Do I need to register?
Answer: EOH is completely free and open to everyone. No registration is required—just show up on Friday and/or Saturday to check out the exhibits.

Question: Where can I find information about specific exhibits?
Answer: Browse every exhibit in the Visitor Hub. During EOH, printed Visitor Guides are also at the Visitor’s Booths.

Question: Will food be available on campus during the event?
Answer: Yes! Food trucks will be located on Mathews Avenue.

Question: Which food trucks will be available?
Answer: Available trucks include Juanitos Tacos, La Paloma, Burrito King, Pastamania, Brien’s Bistro, Smith Burger Co., Kona Ice, Travelin’ Toms Coffee, Urban Oasis, Stango Cuisine, Jurassic Grill, FOUR American Grill, and Fernando's Food Truck.

Question: What should our group plan on doing throughout the day?
Answer: Schools’ schedules are flexible! We recommend checking out our Recommended Events for K-12 Visitors and planning your day around your group’s interests. Example schedule: • 8:00-9:00 AM - Bus to EOH • 9:00-10:00 AM - Explore student exhibits • 10:30-11:00 AM - Watch Illinois Space Society’s Rocket Launch • 11:30 AM-12:00 PM - Drive an Excavator with Caterpillar • 12:00-1:00 PM - Lunch • 1:00-1:30 PM - Learn to Solder • 1:30-2:00 PM - Explore student exhibits • 2:00-2:15 PM - Gather at bus loading zone • 2:15-3:15 PM - Bus back to school

Question: What should our group plan on doing for lunch?
Answer: There are a variety of restaurants and food trucks on campus during EOH! Guests are also welcome to pack lunch and eat around campus at our several designated outdoor areas. There will be tables and tents set up near our food trucks as well as grassy areas for groups to sit. Unfortunately, we cannot assign or guarantee specific locations to specific groups because of the large number of guests attending. There are also indoor eating spaces available in the basement of the Illini Union. See the Food FAQs for the food trucks at EOH. Some Nearby Restaurants (within ~10 minute walk): • Panda Express • Mia Za’s: Pizza, Sandwiches, Pasta • Shawarma Joint: Casual Mediterranean food, chipotle style • Subway • Jimmy Johns • Noodles & Co • Chipotle • Murphy’s: American style pub food • Thai Fusion: Casual Thai food • Atomic Wings: Chicken wings and sandwiches

Question: Where can I park?
Answer: Some lots are open both days, and more open on Saturday. Every lot, with a Google Maps link, is listed under Shuttles & parking.

Question: Is shuttle service available?
Answer: Yes. EOH shuttles loop between parking lots and the exhibit areas on both days. Hours, stops and the route map are under Shuttles & parking.

Question: Where do buses pick up and drop off?
Answer: Drop-off, parking and pick-up directions for school buses are on the Field trips page.

Question: Are there any street closures?
Answer: Yes. From 7:00 am to 6:00 pm, W. Springfield Ave (Wright to Mathews) and S. Mathews St (Green to Springfield) will be closed to all but authorized vehicles.

Question: What is the protocol for a lost or missing child?
Answer: Immediately notify the nearest Visitor’s Booth. A volunteer will bring the child to the Visitor’s Booth in CIF and notify 911. A parent or guardian can meet the child at CIF.

Question: What should I do in case of a medical emergency?
Answer: Notify a nearby volunteer immediately and go to the EMS tent on Graziano Plaza, located between Engineering Hall and Everitt Laboratory.

Question: Which hospitals are nearby?
Answer: Nearby hospitals include Carle Foundation Hospital and OSF HealthCare Sacred Heart Medical Center – Urbana.

Question: What should I do in any other emergency?
Answer: Approach any EOH volunteer in the Visitor’s Booth in the Campus Instructional Facility (CIF).

Question: Is there a Lost & Found?
Answer: Yes. Lost items can be taken to the Visitor’s Booth in CIF (9:00 am–5:00 pm, Friday & Saturday) or to the Engineering Council Office (Engineering Hall 103C) at other times.

Question: How can I identify staff and volunteers?
Answer: Shirt colors indicate roles: Volunteers (Yellow), Exhibitors (Light Pink), Committee Members (White), Sponsors (Latte), Judges (Navy), HSDC (Bright Blue), MSDC (Lavender), Start-Up Showcase (Burgundy), Visitors (Aloe).
